candidate: C1b: ordered descriptor file parallelism on retained CLI/CI commit 3ea936d
decision: Accept this scientifically equivalent bridge for subsequent optimization, retaining substantial C1 batch benefits and the disclosed bounded costs.
next_step: Fresh accepted-C1b diagnostic profile, then pre-edit C2 hypothesis and source freeze.
performance_gate: Every pair improves both file-batch workloads at 2/4/6 threads. Paired median speedups: 10,000 files 1.9368/3.7324/5.4224; 56 files 1.8168/3.0631/4.0055. One-thread large batch remains approximately neutral.
retained_tradeoffs: Parser paired wall regression about 0.9/1.0/1.3 percent at 1/4/6 threads, with corresponding CPU costs; two-thread result approximately neutral.
Some single-file startup measurements are slower, including six-thread-setting single_small by about 5.7 percent (medians 2.256 versus 2.367 ms). This is retained and not called a gain.
Screen paired wall medians are slower at 2/6 threads but CPU approximately neutral; full sample ranges and ordering remain available. No screening gain is claimed.
Search is strongly bimodal, with conflicting paired and ratio-of-median estimates. No precise wall-time gain is claimed; small CPU costs are retained.
Six-thread 10,000-file candidate peak RSS is 26.57 MiB. Parallel batch total CPU increases about 6.4 percent for 10,000 files and 15.4 percent for 56 files.
sample_policy: All 720 launches and 320 alternating measured pairs retained; no exclusions, no changed acceptance threshold, and no old C1 measurements assigned to C1b.
scientific_gate: 128,021 responses exactly equal, all 93 CLI cases at four thread settings, 24 extra CLI bridge cases, all independent references with unchanged limits, full million-value prediction streams, and engineering checks pass before timing.
scope: This receipt covers only the frozen C1b executable. It retains pre-existing commit 3ea936d; it makes no independent speed claim for the CLI argument grouping. All cumulative claims compare to corrected baseline 1ecfbd5. Subsequent incremental comparisons must use this actual C1b executable.
tradeoff_rationale: The multi-second, reproducible file-batch reductions justify the small parser/startup and bounded memory/CPU costs for the intended descriptor batch workloads. Unrelated workloads have no universal speedup claim. Final combined measurements must expose these costs again.
